newsitem.title: UK: Morgan Grenfell awaits ruling on Sysdeco.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Grenfell awaits ruling on Sysdeco.

text.p: Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM), the fund management unit of Deutsche Bank AG, said it is awaiting a ruling by the Norwegian authorities over whether it is legally bound to bid for software company Sysdeco.

A spokesman for MGAM said it holds 20.7 percent of Sysdeco while its parent, Deutsche Bank, holds 26.7 percent. MGAM is arguing that the stakes, amounting to a total 47.4 percent, should not be consolidated.
Under Norwegian law, MGAM/Deutsche might be obliged to formally bid for Sysdeco if the authorities rule that the two holdings should be counted as one.
The other alternative would be for MGAM to sell some shares.
In a statement in September, MGAM/Deutsche said they owned a combined 51.2 percent of Sysdeco.

The spokesman said that recent sales of Sysdeco shares were normal portfolio management adding that Tuesday's sales of 22.1 million shares in British Biotech was to realign the holdings of two of the funds managed by former fund manager Peter Young.
Young was sacked from MGAM after irregularities emerged in his management of the funds. The activities are now under investigation by both the industry regulator IMRO and the Serious Fraud Office.
The MGAM spokesman said the two funds in question continue to hold British Biotech shares as do ther funds controlled by MGAM.
He said the unlisted securities in the funds managed by Young, taken on to Deutsche's books in September at a cost of 180 million stg, were still there, none having been sold.
Figures published this week showed that the MGAM affair caused a big dent in retail sales of UK unit trusts, which fell to 205 million stg in September from 347 million stg in August.
